map.more: {{count}} more nodes. Use the list to see all of them.

models.noneSub: Loaded replicas on healthy nodes appear here.
models.caption: Running models across the cluster
models.stopMessage: {{name}} has {{replicas}} loaded across {{nodes}}. This stops all loaded placements on those nodes.
models.stopFailed: Could not stop {{name}}: {{message}}. Some replicas may already have stopped.

scale.title: Distributed mode is not enabled
scale.sub: Distributed mode spreads models across worker machines and routes requests across them. Start LocalAI with it turned on, then register a worker.

command.copyFailed: Could not copy. Select the text and copy it by hand.

leave.title: What happens if I drain this node
leave.titleDraining: What is affected while it drains
leave.titleLost: What the loss of this node means
leave.empty: Nothing is loaded here and no request is running, so draining changes nothing.
leave.emptyLost: Nothing was loaded on this node, so nothing stops serving.
leave.inflight: {{count}} requests in flight finish first. No new ones are sent here.
leave.inflightLost: {{count}} requests were in flight on this node and cannot finish.
leave.blocked: is unavailable until this node returns: its rule only allows {{selector}} and no other healthy node has those labels.
leave.reload: loads again on the next request on another healthy node that fits. Free memory is not compared here.
leave.reloadNone: has no other healthy node to move to, so it stops until this node returns.
leave.unavailable: The cluster did not return the loaded replicas or the rules, so this cannot be worked out now.
leave.how: Worked out in this browser from the node list, the loaded replicas and the placement rules. The server does not compute it, and the scheduler also weighs free memory and disk when it loads a model.

detail.notFoundSub: It may have been removed from the cluster.
detail.loadFailedSub: The cluster may be temporarily unavailable.
detail.downSub: Figures below are the last it reported. Requests already skip this node.
detail.pendingSub: It gets no requests until you approve it.
detail.drainingSub: It takes no new requests and finishes the ones running. Resume to return it to service.
detail.noModels: No models loaded yet. Replicas appear here when they are scheduled to this node.
detail.placementNote: Where models go is decided by the scheduler and by
detail.backendsSub: Runtime engines available on this node.
detail.backendsFailed: Could not read the backends on this node.
detail.name: Name
detail.logsSub: Logs open per replica, with the output of its backend process.
detail.noLogs: Nothing is loaded here, so there are no process logs.
detail.replicaCapSub: Limit how many replicas of one model may run here.
detail.labelsSub: Labels describe this worker and decide which placement rules may use it.

drain.title: Drain {{name}}?
drain.desc: A draining node takes no new requests. What is running finishes.
drain.undo: You can resume the node at any time.

remove.title: Remove {{name}}?
remove.desc: This deregisters the node from the cluster. A worker that is still running registers again and waits for approval.
remove.impact: {{count}} loaded replicas on this node stop serving.

unload.title: Unload model
unload.busy: "{{name}}" has {{count}} request(s) in flight. Unloading interrupts them. Continue?

backendDelete.title: Delete backend
backendDelete.message: Delete "{{backend}}" from {{node}}? This removes the backend files from this node only.

shrink.title: Reduce replica capacity
shrink.message: {{name}} has {{loaded}} replica(s) of at least one model loaded. Reducing the cap to {{value}} evicts nothing now: running replicas keep going and the reconciler trims them on the next idle window. Continue?

rules.title: Placement rules
rules.lede: Rules say which model may run where. A model without a rule goes wherever the scheduler finds room.
rules.heading: Rules
rules.empty: Add a rule to keep a model on certain nodes, to keep replicas running, or to run it on every node.
rules.byPrefix: It is routed by prefix cache.
rules.shadowedTitle: Another rule already governs the same model, so this one has no effect. Placement decides where a single shared load runs, so only one rule per model can apply.
rules.unsatisfiableTitle: The reconciler could not satisfy this rule (capacity exhausted). It retries by {{when}}, or sooner when a node joins or leaves.

sentence.placement: {{model}} runs as one replica on a node with {{labels}}.
sentence.inactive: {{model}} has no placement of its own: the scheduler decides.

auto.atLeastAny: {{model}} keeps at least {{min}} replicas on any healthy node.
auto.atLeastLabels: {{model}} keeps at least {{min}} replicas on nodes with {{labels}}.
auto.exactlyAny: {{model}} keeps {{min}} replicas on any healthy node.
auto.upToAny: {{model}} runs up to {{max}} replicas on any healthy node.
auto.upToLabels: {{model}} runs up to {{max}} replicas on nodes with {{labels}}.
auto.betweenAny: {{model}} keeps {{min}} to {{max}} replicas on any healthy node.
auto.betweenLabels: {{model}} keeps {{min}} to {{max}} replicas on nodes with {{labels}}.

matrix.title: Placement preview
matrix.caption: Where each rule puts its model, by node
matrix.how: Worked out in this browser from the node list, labels and rules. "Loaded now" is read from the loaded replicas. The scheduler also checks free memory and disk when it loads a model.

sheet.desc: Choose the model, how many replicas, and where.
sheet.modelPlaceholder: Type to search models or aliases, or paste a name…
sheet.aliasNote: {{name}} is an alias for {{target}}. This rule applies to whichever model the alias points at, and follows it if you repoint it.

help.placement: Restrict this model to certain nodes. It loads on demand and can be evicted when idle.
help.spread: Run one replica on every node that matches. With no labels, on every healthy node. It follows nodes joining and leaving.
help.autoscaling: Keep a target number of replicas across the cluster. A minimum of 1 or more protects it from eviction.

sheet.selector: Only on nodes with these labels
sheet.selectorOptional: Only on nodes with these labels (optional)

selectorHelp.placement: The model loads only on nodes that match every label.
selectorHelp.some: Replicas land only on matching nodes.
selectorHelp.empty: No labels means any healthy node.

sheet.routingHelp: Prefix cache sends requests that share a prefix to the same replica to reuse its KV cache, and falls back to round robin when replicas are out of balance.
sheet.minPrefixHelp: Share of the prompt (0 to 1) that must match a cached prefix before affinity applies. 0 inherits the default.
sheet.balanceAbsHelp: Largest in-flight gap allowed before falling back to round robin. 0 inherits the default.
sheet.balanceRelHelp: Largest in-flight ratio (1 or more) allowed before falling back to round robin. 0 inherits the default.

preview.title: Where this rule puts it
preview.pickModel: Pick a model to see where it would go.
preview.noRoster: The node list is not available, so there is nothing to compare.
preview.needLabels: Add at least one label to say which nodes it may use.
preview.none: No healthy node matches {{labels}}. The rule cannot be met until one does.
preview.spread: would run on all {{count}} matching nodes: {{nodes}}.
preview.shortfall: {{count}} more replicas than these nodes can hold under their replica cap.
preview.placement: would load on demand on one of {{count}} matching nodes: {{nodes}}.
preview.how: Worked out in this browser from the node list and labels. The scheduler also checks free memory and disk when it loads a model.

sheet.pickerEmpty: No model matches. "{{name}}" is used as typed.

failover.lede: A failover chain serves one model name from an ordered list of targets and moves requests to the next healthy one. When a worker stops answering, the router and the health monitor already reroute around it.
failover.lostSub: Last heartbeat {{when}}. Requests skip a node that does not answer.

notAnswering.title: Declared not answering
notAnswering.text: After 5 minutes without a heartbeat by default (the stale node threshold). A failed model health check or a failed request notices a lost worker sooner.

requests.title: Requests for its models
requests.text: Go to another node that has the model loaded. If none has it, the router loads it on a node that fits. A request sent to a worker that has gone is retried elsewhere.

replicas.title: Replicas it was running
replicas.text: Placed again on a matching node when a placement rule asks for them. Rules that cannot be met are retried when a node joins or leaves.

back.title: When it comes back
back.text: It takes requests again after its next fresh heartbeat. Its models load again on demand.

failover.policyNote: This describes how the router and the health monitor behave. The timings are server settings that this page does not read.
failover.single_one: {{count}} model runs on a single replica.
failover.single_other: {{count}} models run on a single replica.
failover.singleSub: If its node goes away, it stops until that node returns or a load lands elsewhere.

add.title: Add a node
add.sub: Run one command on the machine you want to add. It appears here by itself.

join.title: How should it join?
join.workerSub: The worker registers with this instance and waits for your approval. It needs the message bus and the database that distributed mode uses.
join.peerSub: Another LocalAI instance joins over P2P and shares its models. Requests are balanced across the instances.
join.shardSub: A machine lends its memory to hold part of one large model. It splits one model across machines instead of spreading requests.

distributed.title: Turn on distributed mode first
distributed.sub: This install runs on one machine. Start it with distributed mode, then add workers.

p2pOff.title: Turn on P2P first
p2pOff.sub: P2P is not enabled on this instance. Start LocalAI with it enabled; it makes a network token that the new machine uses. Reload this page when it runs.

run.title: Run this on the new machine
run.devTitle: Use development (master) images instead of stable releases
run.tokenNote: Set TOKEN to the registration token from the server configuration. This page never shows it.
run.p2pNote: The token is the P2P network token of this instance. Every machine in the network uses the same one.

wait.title: Waiting for the machine
wait.listening: Listening for a worker. This page updates when one registers.
wait.stuck: Nothing arrives? Check that the machine reaches the message bus and that the token matches.
wait.p2pCount: {{count}} peers online. This page updates when another joins.
wait.p2pStuck: Nothing arrives? Check that the machine reaches this network and uses the same token.

p2p.title: P2P
p2p.lede: Peers join this instance over a shared network token. They need no message bus and no database.
p2p.offSub: Turn on peer-to-peer networking to use other machines without a message bus or a database: share whole instances or split one model across machines.

federation.title: Instance federation
federation.text: Balance requests across several LocalAI instances.

sharding.title: Model sharding
sharding.text: Split one large model across workers so it fits.

sharing.title: Resource sharing
sharing.text: Pool the memory and compute of devices you already have.

p2p.enableStart: Start LocalAI with P2P on. It makes a network token for you.
p2p.enableToken: Or start it with a token you already have from another instance.
p2p.enableThen: Reload this page when it runs to see the token and connect machines.
p2p.tokenNote: Every machine in the network uses the same token. Pass it in the TOKEN environment variable.
p2p.federationSub: A federated server is the entry point: it takes API requests and balances them across the federated instances behind it.
p2p.serverSub: Run this on the machine that clients will call. It listens on port 8080 by default.
p2p.port: To change the port, add -e ADDRESS=:9090.
p2p.shardingSub: Federation spreads whole requests. Model sharding splits one model across machines, each holding part of its layers.
p2p.llamaSub: Each worker lends its GPU or CPU memory to hold a share of the model.
p2p.mlxSub: Apple Silicon Macs run the model together over native links.
p2p.shardCommands: The commands to start a worker are in
